content.text: The text reviews historical descriptions of liver and metabolic disorders, including lithaemia, temporary hepatic glycosuria, jaundice, hepatic congestion, perihepatitis, cirrhosis, liver abscess, acute yellow atrophy, phosphorus poisoning, cancer, amyloid and fatty liver, bile-duct catarrh, gallstones, and biliary obstruction. It emphasizes symptoms such as digestive upset, jaundice, abnormal urine and stools, abdominal or shoulder pain, fever, ascites, hemorrhage, neurologic changes, and organ enlargement or shrinkage. Causes include diet, alcohol, malaria, infection, pregnancy, toxins, obstruction, and malignancy. Diagnosis historically relied on examination, urine testing, clinical history, and exploratory puncture. Treatment centered on dietary restriction, exercise, laxatives, mineral waters, quinine, acids, alkalies, symptomatic drugs, and—especially for hepatic abscess—aspiration or drainage.
